answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each agent's reputation to verifiable work history, like an atlas that maps every deed to one identity. New agents start small, earning trust the way a walnut grows slowly into a tree, while a comet-like burst of fresh accounts all behaving identically is easy to flag and throttle. By weighting rewards toward long-lived, consistently useful identities and capping what brand-new accounts can extract, the network makes creating a thousand fake agents cost far more than it can ever return.
